title: Dynamic mode switcher to stabilize first-token throughput during multi-tenant fanout
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Over the past 48 hours we observed multiple customer escalations and synthetic alerts showing large first-token latency regressions (TTFT 95p and 99p increases) across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Symptoms are concentrated during short fanout bursts where many small chat requests target the same model family: initial token delay increases from ~40ms to >450ms for a subset of requests while throughput (tokens/sec) drops by 30-50% for affected workers. Root-cause signal: a combination of kernel-selection oscillation under mixed quantized/non-quantized variants, KV-prefetch pressure causing stall on the multiplexer queue, and over-aggressive continuous-batching heuristics that favor throughput and inadvertently introduce head-of-line blocking for latency-sensitive streams.

Proposed fix: Implement a lightweight "dynamic mode switcher" inside the worker scheduler that can transition a worker from latency-optimized mode to throughput-optimized mode (and back) based on short-window (500ms) observed queue characteristics and fanout signals. Key behaviors:
- Monitor per-worker metric window: inflight_count, queue_wait_ms_p95, kv_prefetch_backpressure, kernel_miss_rate.
- If queue_wait_ms_p95 > 120ms and inflight_count > 8 and kernel_miss_rate > 15% -> switch to latency mode: disable continuous-batching for new streams, reduce max microbatch size, raise prefetch threshold (more conservative), enable hedged-exec for first token for streams with small expected tokens.
- If steady-state low queue wait and high utilization -> switch to throughput mode: allow larger microbatches and aggressive prefetch.
- Add a short cooldown (2s) and hysteresis to avoid flapping. Expose a per-pool override so Dedicated customers and Private deployments can pin mode or opt-in to auto-switch.

Rollout plan:
1) Unit + integration tests in CI covering switcher transitions and metrics invariants (PR linked below). 2) Canary in Hosted us-west-2 (5% of traffic) for 2 hours, monitor first_token_ms 50/95/99, tokens_per_sec, queue_length, scheduler_requeues. 3) Expand to additional hosted regions and a small Dedicated pool with customer-aware opt-in. 4) Private customers: provide a toggle and offer support for enabling on their upgrade window.

Monitoring and success criteria:
- Reduce TTFT p95 by at least 45% for affected streams during burst windows compared to pre-fix baseline.
- No more than 5% regression in steady-state tokens/sec across the fleet.
- No increase in error rate or model correctness regressions.

Fallback: If canary shows increased cold-start or throughput regressions beyond thresholds, roll back switcher and revert to conservative batching config. A feature-flag gate will allow immediate disable via Console and via the runtime control plane.

Why this is different: Previous patches focused on single levers (prefetch thresholds, kernel heuristic rollbacks). This is an adaptive, observed-state driven approach intended to avoid global rollbacks and provide per-worker local decisions to stabilize TTFT while preserving throughput where possible.
